<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:34">Y. Ber. I, 3ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ מלאה וכ׳</he> a basket full of bones.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13">Gen. R. s. 13</cite> <he>הבא קוּפָּתְךָ וכ׳</he> bring thy tub and measure (fill it); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:5:4">Y. Succ. I, 52ᵇ</cite> bot.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 10:2:3">Y. Sabb. X, 12ᶜ</cite> top <he>ק׳ פרוצה</he> a basket which is broken through (the contents of which protrude). Bab.

<cite ref="Gittin 67a:8">Gitt. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>ר׳ יוחנן</he> … <he>קופת הרוכלים</he> R. Joḥ. ben Nuri is a spice-peddlars’ basket (ready in all branches of learning); <he>ר׳ … ק׳ של בשמים</he> R. El. is a spice box; <cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 18:4">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XVIII</cite>; <cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 18:3">ib.</cite> <he>ק׳ של הלכות</he> a basket (or a pile) of laws (an erudite scholar).
Keth. VI, 4 החתן … עשרה דינרין לק׳ וכ׳ the bridegroom must obligate himself to give his wife ten Denars for the ḳuppah for each Maneh (which she brings in), expl.
<cite ref="Ketubot 66b:7">ib. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>ק׳ של בשמים</he> for perfumes; a. v. fr.—
Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. III, 7 קיפה (corr. acc.).—Esp. ḳuppah, the communal fund for dispensing sustenance to the poor every Friday, contrad. to תמחוי.
Peah VIII, 7 לא יטול מן הק׳ must not take support from the ḳuppah; a. e.—Pl. קוּפּוֹת.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 1:4:6">Y. Ab. Zar. I, 39ᵈ</cite> <he>היה למוד … ק׳ והוציא עשר</he> if one was in the habit of exhibiting five baskets with goods, and exhibited ten (on account of the gentile festival).
